questions.questionText: The prize was shared between Anita and ____.
questions.explanation: After a preposition (between), the object form 'me' is used.

questions.questionText: Rahul and ____ went to the market.
questions.explanation: As part of the subject, the subject form 'I' is needed.

questions.questionText: It was ____ who called you yesterday.
questions.explanation: After 'it was' the subject form is used with a following relative clause: he.

questions.questionText: She blamed ____ for the accident.
questions.explanation: The subject and object are the same person, so a reflexive pronoun is needed: herself.
questions.shortcut: Same person doing and receiving = reflexive.

questions.questionText: The book is not mine; it is ____.
questions.explanation: A possessive pronoun standing alone completes the sentence: hers.
questions.shortcut: Possessive pronoun has no noun after it.

questions.questionText: This is ____ umbrella, not yours.
questions.explanation: A possessive adjective is followed by a noun: my umbrella.

questions.questionText: Each of the boys has finished ____ homework.
questions.explanation: 'Each of the boys' is singular and refers to male persons: his.

questions.questionText: The old man lost ____ way in the forest.
questions.explanation: The pronoun must match the singular male subject 'old man': his.

questions.questionText: Kavya and Divya completed ____ projects before the deadline.
questions.explanation: The plural subject takes the plural possessive: their.

questions.questionText: The company has changed ____ policy on refunds.
questions.explanation: A company as one unit is referred to with 'its'.

questions.questionText: He did all the work by ____ without any help.
questions.explanation: 'By himself' means alone; the reflexive follows the preposition when it refers back to the subject.

questions.questionText: Between you and ____, the plan will not work.
questions.explanation: 'Between' is a preposition and takes the object form: me.

questions.questionText: She is not as intelligent as ____ am.
questions.explanation: The verb 'am' needs a subject, so the subject form I is used.

questions.questionText: Do you know ____ is waiting outside?
questions.explanation: 'Who' is the subject of 'is waiting', so the subject form is used.

questions.questionText: To ____ did you give the keys?
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'to', the object form 'whom' is used.

questions.questionText: The man ____ car was stolen reported to the police.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun shows possession of the car, so 'whose'.

questions.questionText: This is the girl ____ won the first prize.
questions.explanation: 'Who' is the subject of 'won'. Persons take who.

questions.questionText: The watch ____ I bought yesterday has stopped.
questions.explanation: The antecedent is a thing, so the relative pronoun 'which' is used; who/whom are for persons.

questions.questionText: He is the man to ____ I gave the money.
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'to', the object form 'whom' is used.

questions.questionText: They enjoyed ____ at the festival.
questions.explanation: The subject and object are the same, so the reflexive 'themselves' is used.

questions.questionText: She prepared the dinner ____.
questions.explanation: Used for emphasis, the reflexive 'herself' follows the noun or the verb phrase.

questions.questionText: The lion hurt ____ while trying to escape the cage.
questions.explanation: A lion as an animal is referred to as 'it', and since the subject and object are the same, 'itself' is required.

questions.questionText: We should respect ____ elders.
questions.explanation: A possessive adjective is needed before the noun 'elders': our.

questions.questionText: The climate of Ooty is cooler than ____ of Chennai.
questions.explanation: 'That' stands for the singular noun 'climate' to avoid repetition.

questions.questionText: The teacher told Meena and ____ to stay back.
questions.explanation: 'Told' takes an object, so the object form 'me' is needed.

questions.questionText: Let you and ____ finish the work first.
questions.explanation: 'Let' takes an object form: let you and me.

questions.questionText: Hari as well as ____ was selected for the camp.
questions.explanation: The pronoun is part of the subject of 'was selected', so the subject form: I.

questions.questionText: Only the two of ____ know the password.
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'of', the object form is used: us.

questions.questionText: The leaves of this plant are bigger than ____ of that plant.
questions.explanation: 'Those' stands for the plural noun 'leaves' to avoid repetition.

questions.questionText: Seema and Reena are friends; ____ love each other.
questions.explanation: A plural subject needed for two girls: they.

questions.questionText: Which of these two bags is ____?
questions.explanation: A standalone possessive pronoun is needed here: yours.

questions.questionText: The students ____ passed the test were awarded certificates.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun refers to persons and is the subject of 'passed': who.

questions.questionText: The old woman ____ I met yesterday is my neighbour.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun is the object of 'met' and refers to a person: whom.
